_rules.OK: converts; dates (count and order), CRS and sampled values equal the independent read of the source, values inside the physical range a scientist expects, longitudes inside +-180 for EPSG:4326
_rules.WRONG: converts but something is wrong: dates, orientation, values, CRS, longitudes beyond +-180, undeclared fill stored as data, scale convention wrong, dropped steps
_rules.ACTIONABLE: refuses, and for every problem reported the message names a fix that clears that problem when applied
_rules.UNACTIONABLE: refuses, and some problem has no named fix, or the named fix does not clear it, or applying it loses data
_rules.CRASH: traceback, unhandled exception or timeout (none occurred)
_rules.first_run: exactly what the docs tell a newcomer: convert INPUT STORE --dry-run, then convert if it passes (plus --variable for NetCDF/Zarr, which convert.md shows)
_rules.after_fix: outcome of the verified fix chain (fixes.json, fix_prep.py); the fix runs use the extras venvs Ax/Bx where the netcdf extra is needed
_rules.A_vs_B: convert, validate and every message are identical in 0.4.1 and main ca799a1: git diff v0.4.1..ca799a1 touches no convert code, only the next-steps lines printed after a conversion
